correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge2\), inverse Lagrange columns have numerator coefficients bounded by binomial coefficients and leading coefficient 1, giving deterministic two-sided comparison of the inverse Frobenius gain with reciprocal chord products. Conditional independence and beta integration give the exact Mellin law; the density of log reciprocal chord is explicit and has exponential tail with constant \(1/\pi\). Its k-fold convolution has \(e^{-y}y^{k-1}/(\pi^k(k-1)!)\) density, which yields the Pareto-log nodal tail. Union bounds transfer the sharp order to the matrix, and layer-cake integration gives exactly for \(s<1/2\). Direct checker passed 1015 supplementary assertions; numerics are not used as proof of infinite conclusions.

value.rationale: The fixed-size square random Fourier sampling model has a natural noise-amplification risk; knowing divergence of the ordinary mean is insufficient for choosing robust loss functionals. The complete sharp fractional-moment threshold and dimension-sensitive log degree describe exactly which losses are integrable and the critical winsorization growth, with explicit nodal surrogate calibration across every \(n\ge2\). This is a motivated, nonroutine full distributional boundary, not an isolated small computation.
